# Draft:Amit Nath Tiwari

----
Amit Nath Tiwari is an Indian politician, social worker, and columnist based in Bihar. He has been associated with political organizations including the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and Shiv Sena. He is known for his participation in political movements in Bihar and for writing opinion columns on political, social, environmental, and child welfare issues in regional Hindi newspapers.
Political career
Tiwari has been active in Bihar politics since the early 2000s. On 11 September 2000, he was appointed as one of the General Secretaries of the youth wing of the Nationalist Congress Party in Bihar. His appointment was part of efforts to strengthen the party organization in the state.
During this period, he participated in several party-led protests. In September 2000, he took part in a sit-in demonstration organized by the NCP in Patna as part of a movement related to Bihar’s reconstruction. On 4 July 2001, he participated in a protest in Bettiah against corruption and land encroachment. In October 2001, he was involved in a youth-led protest in Bettiah raising issues related to inflation, administrative corruption, and unemployment.
In 2010, Tiwari was appointed District President of Shiv Sena for West Champaran district. As district president, he announced and formed a 35-member district executive committee. He was involved in party organizational activities, including press conferences related to assembly elections and the organization of workers’ conferences in Bettiah. He also led a party team that examined issues related to the Guruchurwa railway matter and demanded investigation and administrative action.
Social activities
Tiwari is the founder and chief trustee of the Brahmin Sanskar Manch. He played a role in organizing the organization’s first foundation day event in Bettiah, where issues related to community unity and social participation were discussed.
He has also participated in protest marches organized by the Vipra Kalyan Manch in response to political statements affecting community interests.
Writing and columns
Tiwari has written opinion articles and columns for regional Hindi newspapers. His writings cover topics such as democracy, voter responsibility, historical and social issues, environmental concerns, and child protection.
His published works include articles discussing the condition of democracy, the historical background and land-related issues of Bettiah Raj properties, environmental degradation of regional rivers such as Chandrawat and Dhanauti, and social responsibility toward children and child welfare.
